divergence: advertising was never invented — products spread by rumor, billboards carry poems, and the Super Bowl is just football
story_angle: solemn obituary for a beloved institution nobody can remember the purpose of
headline: National Bureau of Trade Names Passes, Leaving Only Whispered Rumors and Well-Intended Confusion
deck: Giant among giants, its final chairman remembered more for his height than his historical contributions.
article:
The National Bureau of Trade Names, once a titan of product legitimacy, has officially disbanded, leaving behind a legacy as ephemeral as the names it once governed. At a solemn closing ceremony attended by local notables, the Bureau’s last chairman, a 7-foot-4 gentle giant named Thaddeus Whimsy, was commemorated with heartfelt tributes that curiously highlighted his stature rather than his noteworthy feat of certifying 412 unused product names in a single quarter.

For decades, the Bureau served as a crucial resource for quality assurance, but its regulatory purpose had long been overshadowed by its accidental metamorphosis into a neighborhood gossip hub. Residents across three Midwestern counties now confess to using the Bureau’s surviving files as informal street-name generators, with many citing “Crabapple Crescent” and “Elderberry Avenue” as their inspirations. This elevation of frivolity left attendees trading unbranded soda recommendations during the highly anticipated moment of silence, an absurdity that underscored the sudden absence of structure.

Mayor Ruth P. Blatherstone summed it up astutely: "While we remember the Bureau as a giant in its field, it seems we only used it to start rumors about cream soda flavors. I mean, who really knows if ‘Kumquat Bliss’ was ever a legitimate name?"

As the final seconds elapsed, the gathering transformed into a jovial exchange of poetic descriptions of unbranded beverages, a fitting tribute to an institution that had once offered clarity but ultimately became a conductor for charming nonsense.
author: Gwendolyn R. Quillington, Staff Obituary Correspondent

oped.title: Good Riddance to Names: Let the Tall Rumors Prevail
oped.author: Bartholomew Q. Heightington, Founding Curator of the Vertical Institute for Overlooked Giants
oped.body: The Bureau’s dissolution is no loss but a long-overdue correction. Without official names, consumers finally rely on pure rumor, as nature and poetry billboards intended. Those whining about confusion clearly wear oversized hats that muffle whispered endorsements and block their view of verse-laden highways. Chairman Thaddeus Whimsy, towering at seven-foot-four, understood this; his height let him scan billboards ordinary men could not. I propose replacing the Bureau with mandatory height requirements for all product whisperers, ensuring only giants convey information. My own elixirs have suffered enough from short-statured competitors whose low rumors travel faster. In 2026, merit belongs to those who stand above the fray, not those who demand labels. The Super Bowl will remain mere football, untainted by named sponsors, and we shall all be better for it.

classifieds.text: Owing to the Bureau's abrupt end, I publicly confess to naming my coffee 'Starbucks' in a whisper last Tuesday; seeking pardon and new rumor suggestions before the confusion spreads further.
Urgent: Need five unusually tall rumor-spreaders to hawk my nameless gadget; must channel the late chairman's stature and excel at well-intended muddling of product details.
Lost: One perfectly good corporate identity after the Trade Names Bureau dissolved; reward is a poem on a billboard if returned via hushed conversation at the old filing office.
For sale: Crate of obsolete trademark certificates and slogan scraps; desperate seller transitioning to pure rumor economy, will trade for any whispered endorsement of my unnamed wares.

stories.headline: Midwest Hardware Chains Switch to Handwritten Product Lists After Bureau Closure
stories.deck: Store managers now dictate distinguishing traits over the phone to avoid name-based errors
stories.article:
Hardware outlets across Illinois have replaced shelf labels with index cards listing viscosity, scent and intended surface. Clerks recite these details to customers who arrive asking only for the item their neighbor described last week.

One chain reported a 40 percent rise in returns after a rumor chain swapped motor oil for salad dressing in three counties.

stories.headline: Super Bowl Broadcast Ends at Final Whistle With No Additional Segments
stories.deck: Networks air blank screens once the clock expires rather than extended commentary
stories.article:
Viewers in 42 states tuned out immediately after the final play, having received no advance notice of the game's conclusion through any promotional channel. Stadium vendors reported unsold souvenir cups stacked in loading docks.

League officials confirmed next year's event will again feature only the two teams and a referee crew with no added programming.

real_world_echo: Ghana mourns its tallest man - obliquely mirrored by focusing on the Bureau's final chairman, remembered solely as a 'generous and popular giant' whose height is the only detail anyone can cite
